svg.title: The research loop, the gate it re-checks every pass, and the five ways it can end
svg.desc: A call to research_urls, carrying a topic, a list of URLs and both ceilings, first dedupes the URLs while keeping the caller's order, then enters a loop drawn as a dashed container. Each pass begins at a budget gate that checks pages visited against the page limit and words read against the word limit. Past the gate the loop loads the page from cache or browser and extracts it, summarizes it while recording whichever summarizer actually ran, and records the source together with its citations, where a claim carrying no source URL raises rather than being recorded. A rail runs from the record step back to the gate rather than to the top of the loop, because the budget is re-checked before every single page. To the right, under the heading how the pass ends, five chips name the exits: the page limit reached with a count of sources not visited, the word limit reached with the same count, a failure appended to the failures list where one dead link does not end the pass, an ordinary completion where the loop ran out of URLs rather than budget, and a stop because no source could be read at all. The first two leave from the gate and the third from the load step, and all five converge on a single ResearchReport carrying stopped_because alongside the sources, citations, failures and word counts.
svg.text: Many pages, one budget, one report
Every exit from the loop is named in the result, so "it finished" and "it ran out" are told apart.
dedupe the URLs, keeping the caller's order
whichever one actually ran is recorded
record the source, add its citations
a claim with no source URL raises instead
back to the gate for the next URL
one dead link does not end the pass
the loop ran out of URLs, not budget
stopped: no source could be read
stopped_because, sources[], citations[], failures[], words_read, words_returned
